text:
maria: Quick heads-up — during bring-up of GemmaX-7B-v2 on dedicated we see a reproducible style/semantics drift compared to the same seed on Qwen-7B. Not a timeout/quant noise thing, looks like attention pattern mismatch.

maria: Minimal repro: run same prompt batch through both models (fp16, nf4) — GemmaX responses drop factuality on named-entity prompts. Example snippets below.

maria: GemmaX (weird): "The capital of Talaris is Northbay, founded in 1820..."
maria: Qwen (expected): "The capital of Talaris is not real — it's a fictional example; if real, you'd check source X."

tyler: Interesting. Could this be rotary/head-dim mapping? We've had models with different head layouts (interleaved vs contiguous). Any converter logs? @oliver have you seen similar? :thinking_face:

maria: Converter log shows no errors but a suspicious warning: "head_dim != expected_head_dim for attention kernel, applying transpose fallback" — that fallback might reorder KV/rotary embeddings. Full snippet:

```
WARN model-converter: expected head_dim=64, got 64*1.0 (headwise-layout=interleaved)
FALLBACK -> transposed attention weights (preserve matmul shape but head order diff)
```

maria: Also checked tokenizer: vocab mapping normalized but special token IDs differ by +1 vs Qwen on the converted checkpoint (weird). Might be two small mismatches compounding.

oliver: I can try a head-remap script to reorder the weight tensor from interleaved->contiguous. Quick patch I used before:

```
# reorder heads: [num_heads, head_dim] -> permute by chunk
perm = np.arange(num_heads).reshape(num_chunks, -1).T.flatten()
w = w.reshape(num_heads, head_dim)[perm].reshape(original_shape)
```

oliver: That fixed a similar Gemma->Llama mapping once (reduced attention drift).

maria: Nice. Also doing a quick quant vs no-quant compare: nf4 per-channel seems noisier than per-tensor for GemmaX on longprefix prompts. Could be alignment of rotary freq scaling across quant kernels.

sara: I can run a 1k prompt eval (QA + entity prompts) across three variants: (A) converted as-is + nf4 per-channel, (B) head-remap + nf4 per-channel, (C) head-remap + nf4 per-tensor. Will log Rouge/BLEU/factuality percentages and sample diffs. Put the command you want me to use.

maria: Please use this reproduce command:

```
# run eval
python eval/run_batch.py --model-checkpoint /mnt/checkpoints/gemmax-7b-v2/converted \
  --tokenizer /mnt/models/gemmax-tokenizer --dtype fp16 --quant nf4 --quant-mode per_channel \
  --prompts data/eval/entity_prompts.jsonl --out results/gemmax_v2_eval.jsonl
```

maria: Also capture logits for first 32 tokens to inspect rotary phase drift. Save GPT-like sampling (temp=0.0) to compare argmaxes.

tyler: If head-remap helps, we should add a small auto-detect in the converter: compute cross-correlation between attention maps on a synthetic prompt against a known reference (Qwen/Gemma canonical) and try both layouts. If one layout yields higher nll or mismatched attention peaks, emit a warning/suggest remap.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: triggered test-run on dedicated-gpu-42 for job eval/gemmax_v2_test (job id 9876). Logs at https://ci.internal/jobs/9876 :rocket:

oliver: One more quick debug tip: print out rotary phase frequencies and compare elementwise to expected pattern (some models use scaled rotary with headwise scaling). Example check:

```
# check rotary freq
freq = np.linspace(0, head_dim-1, head_dim) / (head_dim/2)
# compare freq * scale against checkpoint metadata['rotary_scale']
```

maria: Thanks — assigning to @sara for the run, @oliver to try remap locally and push a small converter patch if it fixes the eval. I'll collect diffs and open an eval regression ticket if we still see >5% factuality drop. :thumbsup:

sara: starting runs now, ETA ~25m. Will paste combined metrics + few counterexamples when done.

maria: great — if remap fixes, we should add a short unit test in our model-converter verifying head-order invariants for new model recipes.

oliver: agreed. If I get a clean fix I'll raise a PR with tests and the permute util.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: job 9876 finished (status=success) — logs archived.

sara: partial results: (after 27m) baseline (A) factuality 72.1%, (B) 88.4%, (C) 86.9%. Head-remap + per-channel beats baseline by ~16 pts. Pushing full JSON in thread.

maria: that's convincing — good catch everyone. I'll draft an RFC for converter auto-detect + remap heuristics.
